0.0.n: A casual apology, less formal than ごめんなさい.

1.1.n: Marks 私 as the person described as inadequate.

1.2.n: An adjective expressing disappointment in one's ability or performance, used here for self-blame.

1.3.n: Together with に, emphasizes a regrettable cause rather than simple limitation.

1.4.n: Completes ばかりに, linking the speaker's inadequacy to an unspoken bad outcome.

2.0.n: A person's name; the speaker addresses Yu while rejecting her self-blame.

2.1.n: Links Yu to せい to identify whose fault is being discussed.

2.2.n: Assigns responsibility for something bad, but that responsibility is denied here.

2.3.n: A casual contraction of では; with ない, it forms the negative expression is not.

2.4.n: Combines with じゃ to deny that Yu is responsible.

2.5.n: Adds emphasis and reassurance to the denial.

3.0.n: The speaker brings up her own performance to comfort Yu.

3.1.n: Includes the speaker alongside Yu as someone whose performance fell short.

3.2.n: Used with a negative verb to stress that nothing worked.

3.3.n: Past negative of 決まる, used here for moves failing to work as intended.

3.4.n: Ends with a supporting reason, suggesting Yu was not the only one who struggled.

4.0.n: Refers back to the previous speaker's point and agrees with it.

4.1.n: Makes the agreement そうです polite.

4.3.n: The speaker now adds her own experience.

4.4.n: Shows that this speaker also had trouble.

4.5.n: Usually means here, but points to a decisive moment in ここって時.

4.6.n: Casually introduces the idea this is the moment, describing 時.

4.7.n: Together with ここって, refers to the moment when success really mattered.

4.8.n: Marks 時 as when the failed draw happened.

4.9.n: Polite past negative of 引ける, the can-draw form of 引く; cards are understood from context.

5.0.n: Refers to the whole group, including the speaker.

5.1.n: Softens the description of their bad luck.

5.2.n: Pairs with 悪い to describe having unfavorable luck.

5.3.n: Marks 運 as what was bad.

5.4.n: Past form of the adjective 悪い, describing their luck during the game.

5.5.n: Limits the explanation to bad luck rather than poor ability.

5.6.n: Adds politeness after だけ; the past timing is already expressed by 悪かった.

5.7.n: Gives the explanation a reassuring, gently assertive tone.

6.0.n: Connects the bad luck just discussed to the speaker's response.

6.1.n: Invites the others' attention before the excited announcement.

6.3.n: Indicates improvement beyond the current level of draw luck.

6.4.n: A noun from 引く, referring here to the luck or quality of drawing cards.

6.5.n: Marks 引き as what the speaker hopes will improve.

6.6.n: The linking form of 良い used before なる to express improvement.

6.7.n: Combines with 良く to describe a change toward better draws.

6.8.n: With に, follows the desired result to express the goal of an action.

6.9.n: Completes ように, connecting the hoped-for improvement to introducing the secret weapon.

6.10.n: Modifies 兵器 to form the compound 秘密兵器.

6.11.n: In 秘密兵器, figuratively describes a special aid expected to give an advantage.

6.12.n: Marks the secret weapon as what was introduced.

6.13.n: Plain past form of 導入する, meaning to introduce something for use.

6.14.n: A sentence-ending の that adds an explanatory tone to the excited announcement.

0.tip: ごめん is a casual apology suited to people you are close to.

1.tip: ばかりに emphasizes a cause with unfortunate consequences; the consequence is left unsaid here.

2.lit: It isn't Yu's fault, I assure you!
2.tip: Name + のせいじゃない denies that the named person is to blame.

3.lit: For me too, the moves didn't come off at all, and besides…
3.tip: 決まる can mean a move works successfully, not just that something gets decided.

4.lit: That's right; I too couldn't draw at the crucial moment.
4.tip: ここって時 means the crucial moment, rather than a time at this physical location.

5.lit: Everyone's luck was just a little bad, that's all, I assure you.
5.tip: だけ limits the cause to bad luck, reassuring everyone that their ability was not the problem.

6.lit: So, listen! So that card draws become better, I brought in a secret weapon!
6.tip: A desired result followed by ように explains what an action is intended to achieve.
